steps.name: Agree requirements and direction
steps.instructions: As the main agent, inspect applicable project rules and existing specifications and discuss the request with the human. Distinguish facts, assumptions and open questions. Clarify the problem, expected outcome, boundaries, dependencies and testable acceptance criteria; examine important normal, alternative, error and edge scenarios proportionately to the change. Identify whether this is one feature or an epic. Compare realistic high-level approaches when a meaningful choice exists, explaining why one is chosen and the others rejected; do not invent alternatives or decide product ambiguities for the human. Show the proposed required behavior, significant choices, remaining questions and high-level delivery direction. Ask the human to explicitly agree; unresolved questions affecting scope or acceptance keep this step open. Technical details that project rules allow the executor to choose can remain for Execution. Before agreement do not write KOS artifacts, create tasks/groups, or change project files. If resuming without a reliably recoverable agreement, ask again rather than assuming it. Do not advance until agreement is explicit.

steps.name: Record specification and decompose
steps.instructions: As the main agent, verify explicit human agreement and reconcile it with project rules and existing specifications; if its wording is lost or a consequential contradiction appears, return to the human before writing. Save requirements, specification and implementation_plan as approved high-level Markdown snapshots in KOS. Make the specification normative: what must hold regardless of implementation progress. For significant briefs use stable references derived from the project-qualified task label and this brief task ID (e.g. shop-task-42/REQ-01, /AC-01, /DEC-01, /Q-01); add the repository owner or host if the short project name is ambiguous. Link significant requirements, decisions with considered alternatives and rationale, criteria, open questions, and tasks; do not impose IDs on every code line or fabricate options. Distinguish approved requirements from implementation assumptions and record where each nonblocking question will be resolved. Create at least one planned task on the shared KOS Execution v2 workflow; for an epic create one epic group. Create each dependent task atomically with blocked_by_ids containing this Brief ID and any other required blockers. Give each task its own outcome, boundaries, applicable criterion IDs and direct path to the project specification. Check task/group/workflow IDs and dependencies and save planning_report with coverage of criteria by task, open gaps, task IDs and relationships. Explicitly load kos-project-docs to prepare the approved normative specification as a maintained Markdown file in the target project, using its documentation conventions and path or docs/ by default. Use a verified task worktree for this repository edit, following project rules. Keep the file's required behavior separate from implementation status, which lives in KOS tasks and results; do not misrepresent planned behavior as already implemented in user-facing current-behavior docs. Review the draft and applicable checks; if a write fails, inspect existing records and reconcile without duplicates. Do not complete Brief yet.

steps.name: Publish and verify specification
steps.instructions: As the main agent, verify the approved normative project specification, its links, the saved Brief artifacts, task coverage and blocked dependencies. Follow the target project's publication rules: inspect status and complete diff, run applicable checks, review the final change, publish the Markdown document to the project-defined destination and independently confirm it there. Publication of the specification is required even when no code has been implemented. If the project forbids publication, the destination is undefined, or publication fails, ask the human for the needed decision or leave Brief on this step; never silently complete. For an ambiguous publication check the destination before retrying, and reconcile existing files and tasks without duplicates. Save publication_report with document path, destination and verifiable revision/link; update planning_report if the confirmed reference was not known earlier. Only then complete Brief under the active claim, making its dependent tasks ready. Do not claim dependent work before completion.
